scope: Architecture, official documentation and selected source entry points were inspected in the original review. Projects were not all deployed or load tested. This English edition preserves that evidence boundary.

projects.name: LangChain
projects.role: Agent construction and model/tool integration
projects.hook: Assemble a tool-calling loop through common model and tool interfaces.
projects.best_for: A single-agent prototype that later needs memory, structured output or additional control logic.
projects.not_for: Scientific software, HPC scheduling and independent scientific acceptance still need separate implementations.
projects.what_to_read: Quickstart and Tools, followed by Middleware and Memory.
projects.structbio_use: Wrap structure inspection and geometric calculations as tools. Record the input files, selections and actual results.
projects.relations: LangChain agents use LangGraph. Deep Agents adds file, subagent and context-management capabilities above this stack.
projects.status_note: The source snapshot uses create_agent and middleware. Structural-biology applications here are proposed adaptations.

review.position: LangChain provides a higher-level agent and integration layer. Trace how a model message becomes a tool call before adding middleware and state; a large integration catalogue does not establish task success.

components.name: Models and messages
components.responsibility: Adapters normalize messages and tool calls across providers. The application must still check whether a selected model supports the tool calling and output constraints required by the task.

components.name: Tools and schemas
components.responsibility: Python tools expose function descriptions, parameters and outputs. Interface validity does not establish file identity, correct chain selection or numerical validity.

components.name: Agent factory and middleware
components.responsibility: create_agent combines the loop with hooks for application behavior. Follow its model nodes, tool nodes and middleware to understand execution boundaries.

components.name: State runtime
components.responsibility: Agents reuse LangGraph control capabilities. Message history, application state and persistence configuration remain separate concerns.

runtime: Pass the question, task data and permitted tools to the agent.
The model returns an answer or parameterized tool calls; the executor records actual tool observations.
Observations re-enter the model, with middleware controlling context or call policies.
After stopping, the application independently checks artifacts and scientific criteria.
review.state: Keep message history, business task state and scientific artifacts distinct. Store stable artifact references and job IDs for long jobs, and reconcile external operations when resuming.
review.deployment: Start with a Python process, a model service and local tools. Add persistence, remote tools and deployment services as needed. Pin LangChain and runtime versions, and do not mix classic agent APIs with create_agent examples.
review.tradeoffs: Centralized integrations make prototyping quick, but abstraction and dependency layers complicate debugging. Compare direct LangGraph use when precise branch control is essential.
review.exercise: Expose a structure-file inspection function. Test a valid input, an unknown chain and a parse failure, saving parameters and raw observations. Compare fixed execution with model-selected tools.
review.reading_focus: Read the factory, middleware types and tool base interfaces. Locate state updates, error propagation and checks outside the model.

projects.name: LangGraph
projects.role: Stateful agent and workflow orchestration runtime
projects.hook: Represent state, nodes and branches explicitly so code controls execution and recovery.
projects.best_for: Multistep tasks with branches, loops, human review or durable recovery.
projects.not_for: HPC scheduling, scientific acceptance and external side-effect management remain application responsibilities.
projects.what_to_read: The calculator Quickstart, then State, Persistence and Interrupts.
projects.structbio_use: Orchestrate input inspection, computation submission, result collection and validation while retaining job IDs and artifact references.
projects.relations: LangGraph can be used independently. LangChain agents and Deep Agents reuse its runtime; applications need not program all three layers directly.
projects.status_note: Durable recovery requires an appropriate storage/checkpointer configuration. It does not establish exactly-once behavior for external operations.

review.position: LangGraph represents long decision processes through explicit state and graph execution. It supports both agent loops and deterministic nodes. Choose it for control and recovery requirements rather than diagram complexity.

components.name: State and update rules
components.responsibility: Define typed shared keys for messages, plans, candidates and acceptance results. Check merge semantics when concurrent nodes write state.

components.name: Nodes and conditional edges
components.responsibility: Nodes run models, tools or business functions. Edges choose continuation, branching and termination. Separate deterministic transformations from uncertain decisions.

components.name: Execution engine
components.responsibility: The engine advances ready nodes and processes execution events and stopping rules. GPU job and scheduler state still live in external systems.

components.name: Checkpointers and interrupts
components.responsibility: Checkpoints preserve recovery material and interrupts await external input. Resumption does not undo or eliminate external side effects.

runtime: Create stable task, input and expected-artifact identifiers.
Validate inputs, then branch to computation, clarification or stopping.
Tool nodes return artifact references and quality nodes apply independent acceptance rules.
Checkpoint while waiting for jobs or review; reconcile external facts before resuming.
review.state: Graph state and actual scheduler state are different. A run or thread identifier cannot replace an external job ID. Re-executable nodes need operation identities and reconciliation rules.
review.deployment: A local prototype needs the runtime and tools. Durable recovery usually adds a checkpointer and persistent store. Version model services, tool processes, storage and cluster adapters separately.
review.tradeoffs: Explicit branches are testable and errors easier to locate, but developers maintain the state and recovery logic. Excessively fine graphs add overhead to otherwise simple tasks.
review.exercise: Build validation, computation and verification nodes with missing-input and failed-quality branches. Resume mid-run and demonstrate that cached memory cannot substitute for querying the external job.
review.reading_focus: Read StateGraph and execution-engine entry points, then checkpoint interfaces. Identify serializable state and application-defined recovery of external actions.

projects.name: Deep Agents
projects.role: Agent harness with files, context management and subagents
projects.hook: Reuse common agent capabilities while focusing on domain tools.
projects.best_for: Complex-task prototypes requiring file operations, delegated subtasks and long-context management.
projects.not_for: It is not a scientific tool collection. File, shell and subagent access do not establish calculation correctness.
projects.what_to_read: SDK Quickstart, then Backends, Subagents and Context engineering.
projects.structbio_use: Delegate manual reading, plan preparation and reporting, while routing structural computations through controlled tools and independent verification.
projects.relations: Built above LangChain create_agent and the LangGraph runtime, with file and subagent capabilities preconfigured.
projects.status_note: Distinguish the SDK from hosted offerings. Enabled behavior depends on configuration; structural-biology use is a proposed adaptation.

review.position: Deep Agents packages common support capabilities in a higher-level harness. Planning, file context and subagents are composable capabilities, not mandatory sequential stages of every task.

components.name: Agent constructor
components.responsibility: Combines the base agent with middleware, models, tools, backends and subagents. Inspect the constructor to determine what an instance actually enables.

components.name: Files and context
components.responsibility: Filesystem middleware exposes material, notes and intermediate content. Backends determine storage; readable files are not automatically accepted scientific artifacts.

components.name: Subagent delegation
components.responsibility: Middleware organizes subtasks and returns. Specify input, budget and deliverables, and do not treat role dialogue as independent verification.

components.name: Backend protocol
components.responsibility: Backends govern file and execution capabilities. A uniform interface does not imply equivalent isolation, persistence or execution semantics.

runtime: Read the goal and available capabilities, then choose direct handling or a task plan.
Read files for additional material or delegate isolated subproblems.
Run scientific tools through a controlled backend and return observations with file references.
Integrate deliverables, then check file identity, quality and interpretation in the application.
review.state: Context files, long-term storage, subagent workspaces and scientific outputs have different lifecycles. Separate model-authored notes from tool-produced evidence.
review.deployment: SDK, CLI and hosted service are different deployment forms. Fix backend, model and workspace rules before adding sandbox execution; hosted-service behavior cannot be assumed for a local file backend.
review.tradeoffs: Preconfigured capabilities reduce setup work but add default context-management behavior. Diagnose planning, file selection, subagent handoff and computation errors separately.
review.exercise: Restrict a subagent to software-manual research and the main agent to verified tools. Require every report claim to link to a real artifact rather than a subagent completion statement.
review.reading_focus: Follow the constructor, filesystem/subagent middleware and backend protocol. Check capability installation, storage destinations and actual subtask return types.

projects.name: LlamaIndex
projects.role: Data-oriented RAG, agent and workflow toolkit
projects.hook: Turn research material into retrievable context and expose queries as tools.
projects.best_for: Retrieval over papers, tool manuals and research notes, or agents that depend on data context.
projects.not_for: Document retrieval cannot replace coordinate calculations, and indexing does not establish scientific correctness.
projects.what_to_read: Starter Tutorial, followed by Agents, RAG and Workflows.
projects.structbio_use: Retrieve versioned manual passages and structure annotations for the planner; use domain tools for numerical work.
projects.relations: Independent of the LangChain stack. Retrieval can be exposed to another agent as a tool.
projects.status_note: Separate the open-source framework from LlamaParse and other cloud products. The source notes describe an emphasis on parsing and extraction.

review.position: LlamaIndex covers data ingestion, indexing, retrieval and agent-facing queries. Treating retrieval as a tool connects a literature system to a computational agent without conflating the two.

components.name: Documents and nodes
components.responsibility: Organize data into retrievable units with provenance, location and metadata. Chunking determines what context reaches the model.

components.name: Indexes and retrievers
components.responsibility: Indexes organize retrieval; retrievers select candidates. Similarity, reranking and filters affect coverage and do not by themselves establish sufficient evidence.

components.name: Queries and tools
components.responsibility: A query pipeline may return raw evidence, an aggregated summary or a generated answer. Preserve this distinction when exposing it as an agent tool.

components.name: Agents and workflows
components.responsibility: Agents select data or computation tools, while workflows organize events and steps. Scientific coordinate semantics and acceptance criteria remain application-defined.

runtime: Parse papers or manuals, retain provenance and versions, and build an index.
A user query or agent triggers retrieval.
Retrieved passages and citations enter generation or planning.
Run numerical tools and cite literature evidence separately from computational artifacts.
review.state: Separate originals, chunks, vector indexes, retrieval results and conversational memory. Rebuild or update indexes when manuals change, and avoid silently combining old parameter descriptions with new tool versions.
review.deployment: Local ingestion and storage are possible with the open-source framework; cloud parsing products require separate service configuration. Record parser, embedding model, index snapshot, filters and agent configuration.
review.tradeoffs: Useful when data context is complex. The main costs are curation, retrieval quality and citation verification. Decouple retrieval from an execution runtime for hours-long calculations.
review.exercise: Index a structural-analysis manual. Check whether two parameter queries retrieve the correct versioned passages, then invoke retrieval and calculation as distinct tools.
review.reading_focus: Read agent/workflow entry points and retrieval/index base classes. Trace a query to returned evidence and distinguish framework code from separate cloud products.

projects.name: Haystack
projects.role: Component-based RAG, agent and data-processing framework
projects.hook: Control retrieval, routing and generation through explicitly connected components.
projects.best_for: Python applications needing composable retrieval, document processing and tool-using agents.
projects.not_for: Coordinate calculations, domain objects and scientific acceptance need separate implementations.
projects.what_to_read: README documentation and Get Started, then Components, Pipelines and Agents.
projects.structbio_use: Build provenance-aware manual retrieval and connect the retrieved information to a computation plan.
projects.relations: Compare data ingestion with LlamaIndex and component/pipeline expression with LangChain.
projects.status_note: The source README includes lifecycle hooks and skill entry points. Pin the version for concrete APIs.

review.position: Haystack expresses LLM applications as components and connected pipelines. Explicit retrieval, routing, generation and agent steps let developers measure and replace individual stages.

components.name: Components and ports
components.responsibility: Defined inputs and outputs connect components. Port compatibility establishes data transfer, while meaning, provenance and quality remain application obligations.

components.name: Pipeline connections
components.responsibility: Pipelines control data flow among retrieval, reranking, routing and generation stages, enabling stage-specific evaluation.

components.name: Agents and tools
components.responsibility: An agent interacts within a tool set and run conditions. Lifecycle hooks expose execution events but do not provide scientific ground truth.

components.name: Stores and integrations
components.responsibility: Document stores and model connectors supply external capabilities. Record their dependencies, indexes and states separately from the core pipeline.

runtime: Connect loading and retrieval into a minimal testable pipeline.
Inspect actual inputs and outputs at every component.
Use an agent for dynamic tool choice while retaining deterministic processing as components.
Record the generated result and its evidence, then apply task-specific checks.
review.state: Pipeline configuration, document stores, model context and tool artifacts are distinct layers. Save the full pipeline and external index snapshot to reproduce version-dependent behavior.
review.deployment: Python prototypes can run locally. Production adds model and document services. Pin integration and core packages separately; an example does not establish backend interchangeability.
review.tradeoffs: Modularity supports substitution and measurement but increases data-connection and type-management work. Scientific computation additionally needs domain tools and job adapters.
review.exercise: Build retrieval, parameter explanation and computation stages. Evaluate correct retrieval, version-compatible parameters and independently verified numerical results separately.
review.reading_focus: Start at Pipeline execution, the Agent component and Tool interfaces. Identify when data reaches the model and how component errors propagate.

projects.name: CrewAI
projects.role: Role collaboration and event-driven workflow framework
projects.hook: Use Agents, Tasks and Crews for collaboration and Flows for explicit control.
projects.best_for: Collaboration with clear responsibilities and deliverables, or applications mixing agent decisions and deterministic steps.
projects.not_for: More roles do not establish scientific correctness. Shared state, external jobs and validation rules need explicit design.
projects.what_to_read: The README distinction between Crews and Flows, then Getting Started and a minimal task example.
projects.structbio_use: Separate manual retrieval, tool planning and reporting, handing off artifacts and verification results.
projects.relations: Crews organize role collaboration; Flows organize events and state control. Compare this with graph-based orchestration.
projects.status_note: Distinguish the open-source framework from its commercial control platform. Compare single-agent and collaborative variants under equal budgets.

review.position: CrewAI organizes agents through roles, tasks and crews, with Flows supplying event-driven control. Understanding these responsibilities is more useful than defining multiple personas alone.

components.name: Agent roles
components.responsibility: Configure goals, tools and models. A role name does not define permitted data or a checkable deliverable.

components.name: Tasks and deliverables
components.responsibility: Specify requirements, dependencies and expected outputs. Reliable collaboration requires artifacts that can be checked rather than trust in another role’s prose.

components.name: Crew collaboration
components.responsibility: Sequential work, delegation and collaboration incur different context and communication costs. Measure benefits under matched budgets.

components.name: Flow state control
components.responsibility: Flows organize deterministic control through events and state, invoking agents or crews where needed. Keep critical control outside free-form conversation.

runtime: Decompose the user goal into tasks with defined inputs and deliverables.
Advance deterministic steps through a Flow and invoke agents where decisions are needed.
Roles use tools and submit agreed artifacts for subsequent roles.
Aggregate a report and independently evaluate artifacts and failures.
review.state: Store role context, task outputs and Flow state separately. Concurrent updates need ownership and version rules. Model reflections should not automatically become persistent facts.
review.deployment: The open-source framework supports local code prototypes; hosted and commercial control capabilities are separate. Record models, tools, task descriptions, collaboration mode and enabled platform features.
review.tradeoffs: Explicit division of labor can be convenient, but communication and context management add cost. Without checkable handoffs, roles can amplify the same error.
review.exercise: Split manual retrieval, tool planning and reporting into tasks. Compare against one agent with the same model and budget using final scientific acceptance as the outcome.
review.reading_focus: Read Agent, Crew and Flow entry points. Locate completion conditions, structured outputs and error propagation rather than only role prompts.

projects.name: PydanticAI
projects.role: Typed Python AI SDK with dependency and output contracts
projects.hook: Connect tools, injected context and typed outputs within an agent loop.
projects.best_for: Python agents that need explicit interface types, structured outputs and controlled application dependencies.
projects.not_for: Type validity does not establish correct biological objects, physical assumptions or numerical results.
projects.what_to_read: A minimal README agent, then Agent, Tools, Dependencies and Output.
projects.structbio_use: Type structure-inspection inputs, dependency context and results, and connect independent domain validation functions.
projects.relations: PydanticAI is an agent SDK. Pydantic provides related data constraints; they solve different problems.
projects.status_note: The source project also includes harness capabilities. Check Evals, Graph and other components separately.

review.position: PydanticAI connects models, tools, dependencies and outputs through a typed loop. Its value is placing contracts in inspectable code, beyond formatting the final answer.

components.name: Agent and run graph
components.responsibility: Define the model, tools and output contract. Distinguish final results from tool observations while following model and tool nodes.

components.name: Dependency context
components.responsibility: Pass databases, services and business objects to tools without putting every resource in the prompt. Manage resource lifetimes separately from conversation state.

components.name: Tools and output types
components.responsibility: Types and validators constrain parameters and final outputs. Parsing failures can trigger handling, but these checks do not establish scientific semantics.

components.name: Graph, Evals and related components
components.responsibility: Control, evaluation, persistence and harness functions occupy separate layers. Selecting one does not supply a complete production system.

runtime: Define task inputs, dependency context and acceptable output types.
Validate parameters before running a model-selected function.
Return structured observations or recognizable errors to the loop.
Type-check the final output, then perform artifact and scientific acceptance checks.
review.state: Separate type definitions, run messages, injected dependencies and scientific data. Serializing an object does not restore external connections. Preserve file and version references alongside model summaries.
review.deployment: Use the Python SDK in an application process and add model services, databases or durable backends as required. Pin Pydantic versions, model capabilities and optional components.
review.tradeoffs: Clear contracts aid tests and refactoring, but overly broad types can hide semantic mistakes. Compare explicit graph control for complex branches and avoid unnecessary components for simple agents.
review.exercise: Represent invalid input, computation failure and failed quality acceptance with distinct result types. Confirm that callers cannot mistake any of them for successful analysis.
review.reading_focus: Trace the run graph to tool definitions and output handling. Separate errors detected by parsers from those requiring domain functions and independent criteria.

projects.name: smolagents
projects.role: Lightweight agent library using code as actions
projects.hook: Let the model compose tools in executable code, then reason from observations.
projects.best_for: Learning code-action agents, tool composition and a relatively small execution loop.
projects.not_for: Generated code is not scientific verification. Execution environment, dependencies and permitted scope require explicit configuration.
projects.what_to_read: README Quick demo, then the CodeAgent loop and tool interfaces in agents.py.
projects.structbio_use: Compose structure-inspection functions under explicit input and tool boundaries, preserving code, parameters and results.
projects.relations: Multiple model and tool sources make it useful for comparison with function-calling SDKs.
projects.status_note: Code actions and software-development coding agents are different concepts. Execution mode depends on configuration.

review.position: smolagents emphasizes code as an action representation. A program fragment can combine several tools more compactly than individual JSON calls, making the executor a critical system component.

components.name: Model and agent loop
components.responsibility: The agent maintains the task and observations. Compare CodeAgent actions with function-call actions to understand debugging and execution differences.

components.name: Tool collection
components.responsibility: Local, Hub or protocol-adapted tools offer bounded external capabilities. Inspect actual dependencies, I/O and versions regardless of the source.

components.name: Code executor
components.responsibility: The executor controls where code runs and what it can access. Correct generated syntax does not establish correct environments or file selections.

components.name: Step and result records
components.responsibility: Logs reconstruct actions, errors and observations. Map code to real inputs, artifact versions and validation records for scientific tasks.

runtime: Provide a task and an explicitly selected tool collection.
Generate code or another supported action and run it through the executor.
Return observations, errors and variable results.
Decide whether to continue, then independently verify final artifacts and calculations.
review.state: Interpreter variables, files, conversation traces and external services have different persistence. An in-memory variable cannot be the sole recovery record for a long job.
review.deployment: Use a local or remote model with the chosen local or isolated executor. Pin model, tool packages, imports and environment; executors need not expose equivalent capabilities.
review.tradeoffs: Code actions express loops and composition compactly but require simultaneous debugging of decision logic and execution environment. Compare with strict function tools under matched tasks and budgets.
review.exercise: Compose two read-only inspection tools, inject a missing file, and inspect how the error informs the next action. Verify final numbers with an independent reference.
review.reading_focus: Read the action loop in agents.py and executor interfaces. Distinguish generated code, code actually executed and actual tool return values.

projects.role: Code-first agent, workflow and task-delegation framework
projects.hook: Put agents, tools and stateful workflows into a testable runtime.
projects.best_for: Modular agent systems, branching state or Google-service integration while retaining model choice.
projects.not_for: The runtime does not supply structural-computation environments, HPC capacity or independent domain acceptance.
projects.what_to_read: The basic README agent, followed by Workflow Runtime, Task API and official recipes.
projects.structbio_use: Organize file inspection, computation calls and deliverables with explicit run state and structural selections.
projects.relations: A code-first alternative to other agent frameworks. Its stated model and deployment flexibility is broader than Gemini alone.
projects.status_note: The source README describes ADK 2.0. Verify the version of older workflow examples before combining APIs.

review.position: Google ADK provides code-first agents, workflows, delegation and development runtime components. Its Google integrations do not imply a single supported model or deployment setting.

components.name: Agents and tools
components.responsibility: Instructions, model configuration and permitted tools define an agent. Test model decision capability separately from real tool execution.

components.name: Runner and sessions
components.responsibility: The runner connects agents, sessions and events. Conversation identity does not replace external task or job identity.

components.name: Workflow runtime
components.responsibility: Sequential steps, routing, loops, parallelism and recovery express control. Inspect actual state and retry configuration instead of relying on a workflow label.

components.name: Task delegation
components.responsibility: Delegated tasks need defined inputs, acceptance, cancellation and completion semantics rather than only a broad natural-language goal.

runtime: Create agents, sessions and task context.
Advance events and model calls through the runner, selecting tools or delegated tasks.
Use workflow state to coordinate subsequent nodes and collect results.
Check scientific results and provenance after collecting events and artifacts.
review.state: Link session messages, run events, workflow state and external jobs without conflating them. Long tasks need stable references; session records need not contain all scientific evidence.
review.deployment: Local development, containers and managed environments are distinct forms. Pin ADK and model adapters; do not mix 2.0 runtime examples with older tutorial APIs.
review.tradeoffs: Useful for modular agents and workflows, especially with Google services. Developers must understand framework run objects and local/cloud configuration differences.
review.exercise: Implement inspection, computation and reporting nodes. Test missing input and a tool failure, checking that the event chain preserves both errors.
review.reading_focus: Start at llm_agent and Runner, then sessions and workflows. Identify when events are emitted, who owns state and how completion is declared.

projects.role: Cross-language agents and collaborative graph workflows
projects.hook: Connect model agents and stateful workflows through consistent development interfaces.
projects.best_for: Applications requiring Python/.NET, explicit collaboration patterns, durable state or Microsoft-service integration.
projects.not_for: Checkpoints do not automatically make external computations exactly-once. Cluster job state and scientific quality still need verification.
projects.what_to_read: The basic README agent, workflow examples, Observability and migration guides.
projects.structbio_use: Represent analysis, job-status and verification nodes while storing task, artifact and review state.
projects.relations: Official migration material links AutoGen and Semantic Kernel to the newer framework. Read historical papers, projects and current APIs separately.
projects.status_note: The source README covers local and cloud modes. Model and hosted capabilities depend on configuration.

review.position: Microsoft Agent Framework combines agents and collaborative graph workflows in a cross-language development system. Understand current interfaces alongside migration from AutoGen and Semantic Kernel.

components.name: Agents and model clients
components.responsibility: Clients connect models and tools with language- and backend-specific configuration. Azure examples do not imply Azure-only execution.

components.name: Function tools and middleware
components.responsibility: Tools provide application actions and middleware handles requests, responses and errors. Separate interface behavior from scientific validation.

components.name: Workflows and executors
components.responsibility: Sequential, concurrent, handoff and team relationships require explicit executor I/O and state, beyond role prompts.

components.name: Checkpoints and observability
components.responsibility: Checkpoints, streamed events and traces support run management. The application still integrates external job submission, reconciliation and artifact acceptance.

runtime: Create model clients, agents and permitted tools.
Run an agent directly or place it in a workflow executor.
Advance execution, handoffs or human input through events and state.
Collect artifacts, reconcile external facts and report supported conclusions.
review.state: Separate framework state, client sessions, traces and external business objects. Recovery uses saved material and does not prove whether a remote job ran or completed correctly.
review.deployment: Choose language bindings and configure model and hosting backends independently. Do not mix experimental modules, stable packages and older project APIs.
review.tradeoffs: Cross-language integration and explicit collaboration patterns are strengths. The wider service/runtime stack introduces more client, configuration and lifecycle concepts.
review.exercise: Complete a task with a local tool, then compare sequential and concurrent workflows. Record actual tool start/end events and validation, and check for repeated external actions after resumption.
review.reading_focus: Read _agents and _tools, then workflow executors and checkpoints. Compare old concepts through migration guides rather than mechanically renaming packages.

components.name: Application and flow definitions
components.responsibility: The UI edits applications, nodes and connections; the backend turns configuration into runs. Identify the executable operation and parameters behind each canvas node.

components.name: Workflow and tool execution
components.responsibility: Models, retrieval and external tools return different outputs. Surface tool failure, node failure and generated-answer failure separately.

components.name: Knowledge, models and services
components.responsibility: Model management, retrieval, plugins and tools supply external capabilities. Their boundaries differ from task state, logs and artifact storage.

runtime: Configure inputs, models and tools in an application or workflow.
Accept a user request through the application API.
Advance backend nodes, record execution events and collect external observations.
Return results through the UI/API while the scientific backend checks objects, files and quality.
review.state: Version applications, run state, knowledge indexes and user files independently. Results from edited flows and older configurations are different experimental conditions.

review.reading_focus: Follow workflow_entry to node execution and events, then compare with canvas configuration. Trace application versions to actual execution parameters.

projects.best_for: Studying visual nodes, graph execution and application interfaces.

review.position: The reviewed Flowise repository was archived. This guide uses it to study the connection between visual nodes, graph configuration and application services, not as a default maintained deployment choice.

components.name: Visual canvas
components.responsibility: Users connect models, tools and flow nodes. A visual connection becomes executable only when types, variables and ordering are interpreted correctly.

components.name: Nodes and backend execution
components.responsibility: Each node needs an implementation and the server executes the configured graph. Inspect how configuration becomes real calls rather than treating screenshots as architecture.

projects.name: Temporal Python SDK
projects.role: Durable workflow and activity runtime
projects.hook: Separate replayable control logic from activities that perform external operations.
projects.best_for: Long-running tasks and cross-service processes with explicit recovery requirements.
projects.not_for: It does not replace scientific scheduling. Durability does not ensure exactly-once external execution or scientific quality.
projects.what_to_read: Official Workflow, Activity and Worker examples, focusing on replay versus external side effects.
projects.structbio_use: Test a simulated long computation through disconnects, retries and cancellation, reconciling an existing job before resubmission.
projects.relations: Workflow histories, activity attempts, scheduler jobs and artifacts have separate identities.
projects.status_note: This is durable-execution infrastructure rather than an agent framework or domain validator.

review.position: Temporal provides durable workflows and activity execution. The core distinction is replayable control versus activities with real external side effects, with scientific schedulers remaining separate.

components.name: Workflows and history
components.responsibility: Control is recovered from historical events. Determinism and code evolution affect safe replay of existing tasks.

components.name: Activities and workers
components.responsibility: Activities perform I/O or computation and workers execute them. Retried activities can repeat, requiring external operation identity and deduplication/reconciliation.

components.name: Timeouts, retries and cancellation
components.responsibility: Policies govern failures and lifecycle, but heartbeats and cancellation require cooperation from activities and external software.

runtime: Submit a workflow and persist its input.
Execute activities, submitting cluster jobs where needed.
Query external status or report progress while control advances.
Recover from history, reconcile real jobs and artifacts, then decide whether to retry.
review.state: Distinguish workflow history, activity attempts, scheduler job IDs and scientific artifacts. Persistent execution does not establish external exactly-once behavior or valid science.
review.deployment: Requires a Temporal service, workers and actual tool or cluster connections. Prototype with a local service and short tasks to test recovery semantics.
review.tradeoffs: Useful for hour-scale and cross-service work, with added service, worker and version-management cost. Short deterministic tasks may not need this platform.
review.exercise: Simulate lost contact, activity retries and cancellation. Query an existing job before retrying, proving that missing acknowledgement alone does not cause duplicate submission.
review.reading_focus: Read workflow, activity and worker examples together, identifying replayable code and actual side effects.

projects.name: A2A Protocol
projects.role: Interoperable task exchange between agent applications
projects.hook: Delegate tasks to remote agents through explicit capabilities, states and artifacts.
projects.best_for: Treating remote agents as black-box services with structured task and result exchange.
projects.not_for: The protocol does not define internal reasoning or establish trusted scientific behavior. A deterministic function often needs only a tool interface.
projects.what_to_read: Protocol lifecycle and data structures, then SDK examples and comparison with MCP.
projects.structbio_use: Specify a remote structure-inspection task with file identity, acceptance rules, waiting states and artifacts.
projects.relations: A2A targets agent-task interoperability, while MCP targets tool-service interaction; the responsibilities differ.
projects.status_note: Read specification, SDK and application backend separately. A protocol repository is not a complete agent framework.

review.position: A2A standardizes tasks and results between agent applications, especially black-box remote services. It differs from tool-oriented MCP and does not prescribe internal decision mechanisms.

components.name: Capability discovery
components.responsibility: Descriptions advertise supported tasks and interfaces. Match them to deployed versions and actual availability.

components.name: Tasks and states
components.responsibility: Manage submission, progress, input requests and completion. Associate reported status with real execution rather than natural-language claims alone.

components.name: Messages and artifacts
components.responsibility: Messages carry interaction and artifacts carry deliverables. Callers still verify files, provenance, object identity and acceptance criteria.

runtime: Discover capabilities and confirm task scope.
Submit inputs and explicit output requirements.
Handle status updates or requests for more input.
Collect and independently accept artifacts without assuming the remote implementation.
review.state: Correlate local tasks, remote Task IDs, messages and artifacts. Protocol compatibility does not imply equivalent costs, states or scientific semantics.
review.deployment: Provide matching protocol versions, client/server implementations and network endpoints. Separate protocol material from the full application backend.
review.tradeoffs: Reduces coupling in remote delegation but adds capability and status trust questions. Direct tool calls are often simpler for one deterministic function.
review.exercise: Write a remote inspection contract covering files, criteria, waiting and deliverables, and explain why plain chat messages would omit important execution semantics.
review.reading_focus: Compare A2A task handoff and MCP tool calls through their lifecycles and data structures before studying SDK examples.
